subject: ela
intro: Twelfth graders cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of an informational text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain. They recognize when a text acknowledges its own limits or open questions.

items.prompt:
Read.

The survey reports that 70% favor the plan, but notes that only 200 people, all from one city, were asked.

Where does the text leave a matter UNCERTAIN?

steps: The sample is tiny and not representative.
So whether 70% reflects the wider public is uncertain.
solution.answer: Whether the 70% reflects the broader public, given the small, local sample.

items.prompt:
Read.

The new drug and the patients' recovery coincided, but patients also changed their diets.

What does the text leave uncertain?

steps: Two factors changed at once, so the cause is unclear.
So whether the drug or the diet caused the recovery is uncertain.
solution.answer: Whether the drug or the diet change caused the recovery.

items.prompt: Why do credible texts sometimes flag UNCERTAINTY?

steps: Acknowledging limits is honest and precise.
So it makes the text more credible.
solution.answer: It makes the text more credible and precise.

items.prompt: When a text flags what is not yet known, it marks ____.
The most convincing proof is the ____ evidence.
An inference is a conclusion drawn from ____.
